integrate.idea: Interpolation census pre-gate: a mechanical script that classifies EVERY {…} interpolation in generate_html and render_project_window_html (and confirms _PROJECT_WINDOW_JS has zero) as data/flag/markup-emitting, with counts, run BEFORE wave sizing; the ≥7,000-line shrink target becomes a derived number from the census, and the extraction wave is gated on the census output, not on hope.
integrate.note: Directly disposes FM-1; receipt: the f-string spans 10966–13671 with real {expr} interpolations — their true character is currently unmeasured.

integrate.idea: Byte-parity golden-file gate for the extraction: a build/test step renders the page via the OLD f-string path and the NEW static-file+bootstrap path and diffs the emitted JS/CSS byte-for-byte (post-de-escaping of {{/}}); Playwright is reserved for the one thing that genuinely changed — the bootstrap-JSON seam.
integrate.note: FM-2 mitigation: makes parity byte-verifiable, not vibe-verifiable; the two-page smoke can't catch dock/paste/drag regressions but a byte diff can't miss them.

integrate.idea: window.ANCHOR_BOOT bootstrap JSON contract: a single small server-injected JSON object (token presence, project id, build id, feature flags, initial counts) is the ONLY server→client state channel; everything else in the extracted JS reads from it or from existing API calls; the contract is a documented, versioned dict in one module.
integrate.note: North Star names 'a small bootstrap JSON' — this makes it a reviewable contract instead of ad-hoc globals.

integrate.idea: Anchor-based slicing, never line numbers: the implementation plan encodes extraction targets as structural anchors (the _PROJECT_WINDOW_JS assignment, the generate_html def, sentinel comments inserted in a tiny pre-wave commit) plus a freshness gate that re-locates each anchor and fails loudly on ambiguity before EXECUTE.
integrate.note: FM-14: the file WILL drift between Stage 2 and EXECUTE (parked ship-v1 build, hotfixes); line 5623 is fiction by then.

integrate.idea: One-time Playwright investment before wave 1: scripted flows for the top-5 stateful behaviors (terminal open+type via stub PTY, pending-paste flush, drag-to-group, maximize/restore, v12 dock click) that run in the extraction gate AND remain as permanent regression assets for every later pillar.
integrate.note: FM-2; receipt: these five flows are exactly the ones the existing two-page smoke never exercises, and C2's cookie flip + C4's re-attach will need the same harness — triple use.

integrate.idea: Serve the extracted frontend through the EXISTING traversal-safe asset-route idiom (resolve()+relative_to, ValueError→None) already proven 4× in the repo (anchor_term_asset 678, xterm_asset 707, brand_asset 743, katex_asset) — one new static root, zero new security surface.
integrate.note: Reuses a battle-tested pattern; the North Star names this idiom explicitly.

integrate.idea: Content-hash cache-busting on the new static files (?v=<hash8> minted at startup from the file bytes), so a deploy always invalidates John's long-lived tabs and the documented stale-browser pitfall doesn't gain a static-file flavor.
integrate.note: FM-12 adjacent; the server currently sends no-cache headers on the monolithic page — static files change the caching story and must not regress it.

integrate.idea: Frontend↔backend contract versioning shim shipped in the LAST pre-migration release: ANCHOR_BOOT carries a build id, every _postJson sends it, the server answers a mismatch with a structured 409 the old client renders as a 'reload required' banner — so no later wave can strand a stale tab or PWA-cached iPad client.
integrate.note: FM-12: the shim must predate every flip; it is tiny and pays for itself the first time a route changes under an open tab.

integrate.idea: Soft merge-freeze on anchor_gui.py declared for the extraction wave specifically, coordinated with the parked ship-Anchor-v1 build's schedule — the one wave that cannot tolerate concurrent drift gets the one narrow freeze, keeping the no-multi-day-freeze rule intact for everything else.
integrate.note: FM-14 second half; a file-scoped soak of days, not a project freeze — compatible with the C7 constraint.

integrate.idea: Route table where EVERY route — including streaming/upgrade specials — has a ROW (method, pattern, auth policy, handler kind: standard|stream|upgrade); the default-deny audit runs over rows; dispatch for kind≠standard is honestly special-cased at the pre-dispatch hook with the row's auth check invoked FIRST. The auditable invariant is 'no route exists without a declared row', not 'one dispatch shape'.
integrate.note: FM-16: term_ws (14223) and term_stream2 (14230) are already pre-dispatch specials; forcing them through a request-response shape would break 401-before-101.

integrate.idea: Explicit 401-before-101 regression test for term_ws: an unauthenticated upgrade attempt must receive 401 before any 101/handshake bytes, asserted at the socket level — preserving the existing hand-rolled RFC-6455 ordering through the table migration.
integrate.note: FM-16; the two most sensitive routes must be the two the audit provably governs.

integrate.idea: ANCHOR_AUTH_WARN log-only mode: each route batch flips to 'warn' first (log who WOULD 401, allow through) for a soak day on the live service, then to 'enforce' — with the warn log reviewed as a gate artifact before enforcement.
integrate.note: FM-4: observes the healthcheck's 5AM walk, CLI mirror, launchers, and any forgotten script before anyone gets a 401.

integrate.idea: Consumer enumeration pre-work: grep-driven inventory of every caller of every currently-open route (repo code, anchor_healthcheck.py's endpoint walk, .bat/.vbs launchers, scheduled tasks, personal scripts dir) and give each a token path FIRST — Authorization header accepted everywhere, ?token= retained only for WS/SSE.
integrate.note: FM-4; bounded work — the open GET plane is 9 named routes and the consumer set is mostly in-repo.

integrate.idea: Cookie-through-WS-upgrade spike on the REAL clients (desktop browser + iPhone PWA over Tailscale HTTPS) before committing D3's cookie wording — verifying the Cookie header survives the ws:// upgrade and SameSite settings on both, with ?token= as the declared WS fallback if it doesn't.
integrate.note: FM-4 tail risk; the anchor-as-app research already targets iPhone/Tailscale, so the PWA client is a known future consumer, not hypothetical.

integrate.idea: Ops-cutover gate with teeth: the C2 wave is not DONE until a healthcheck probe asserts the LIVE :8777 returns 401 on tokenless /api/rnd/projects — i.e. mint token → set NSSM AppEnvironmentExtra → restart → live assert. If John declines to run tokened, that is recorded as a North-Star amendment, never silently.
integrate.note: FM-3: default-deny that evaluates to allow-all on the only deployment that matters is a checkbox, not security.

integrate.idea: Strangler dispatch with fallthrough: the table dispatches first; unmatched requests fall through to the legacy if-elif chains; branches migrate in small reviewed batches; a coverage test counts remaining legacy arms so progress is measurable and the audit knows what the table does NOT yet govern.
integrate.note: D3 mandates strangler-style; the arm-count test turns 'migration in progress' into a number.

integrate.idea: Handlers become module-level functions as they migrate into the table — which kills the os/datetime in-branch import shadowing class (14506, 16063, 15019, 16911) as a free structural consequence; add a distro.py-style AST scan that fails on any in-method import shadowing a module-level name so the class can't return.
integrate.note: C2 names 'zero in-branch imports shadowing module names'; the scan makes it enforced-by-construction, matching the pillar's own philosophy.

integrate.idea: The reviewed open-allowlist as a checked-in artifact: a short OPEN_ROUTES table in the route module with a mandatory justification string per entry, plus a test asserting the set matches exactly — any new open route requires editing the reviewed file, making review structural.
integrate.note: Turns 'explicit, reviewed allowlist' from process into code.

integrate.idea: journal.py with ONE emit() choke point: all appends go through a single function (schema validation, seq assignment, atomic append under WRITE_LOCK); a distro.py-style scan forbids json.dump/open-for-write to journal paths outside the module, and blessed legacy-store wrappers are the only places emit() is called from.
integrate.note: FM-5 structural fix: instrumentation-by-choke-point instead of instrumentation-by-hunting.

integrate.idea: Write-site tripwire to discover the TRUE mutation set mechanically: a test-mode wrapper around file writes under .anchor/ that fails any test whose mutation did NOT append a journal event (journal itself allowlisted); run the full suite + healthcheck under it to enumerate write sites BEFORE designing instrumentation, and keep it running forever as the completeness gate.
integrate.note: FM-5: inverts discovery — the 'half-dozen missed write sites' (direct index.json touches in anchor_gui, rnd_registry lifecycle, boneyard callers) get found by machine, not memory.

integrate.idea: Journal-first write order by decree: emit the event, THEN write the legacy store — an orphaned journal event is a benign 'intent' record, while the reverse orphan is a lost event; document 'journal-ahead' as expected crash residue with an idempotent replay path.
integrate.note: FM-6 first half: fixes the crash-window semantics so divergence has a defined meaning.

integrate.idea: Quiescent, classifying parity gate: the healthcheck derives views from a WRITE_LOCK-bracketed snapshot copy, tolerates a bounded tail window of recent events, and classifies divergence (journal-ahead=OK/crash-residue, legacy-ahead=BUG, conflict=BUG) instead of binary zero/nonzero — with a reconcile-report tool shipped alongside.
integrate.note: FM-6 second half: 'zero divergence' stays meaningful under live concurrent writes instead of becoming known-flaky noise.

integrate.idea: Butler-shaped event envelope, reserve-and-ignore: mandatory correlation_id, causation_id, actor{kind,id} (user-click | auto-advance | healthcheck-synthetic | cli), monotonic per-project seq + wall ts, schema_ver — validated against three concrete written Butler user stories ('what happened on project X this week', 'what did the user decide vs auto-advance', 'which job produced this doc') answerable from envelope fields alone.
integrate.note: FM-13: the parity gate alone would shape a schema that rots; the Butler is the journal's real customer and its stories cost one page now vs a backfill migration later.

integrate.idea: Schema-evolution rule as a binding convention in the journal module docstring: additive-only within a major schema_ver, unknown-field-tolerant readers, and a test that round-trips a v1 event through the v-current reader.
integrate.note: FM-13 tail: makes schema_ver=2 an addition, not a rewrite.

integrate.idea: Recovery tool as a first-class deliverable: rebuild_index.py re-derives a deleted/torn index.json (and sessions.json rows) from the journal, proven in a test that deletes the index mid-suite and in a documented operator runbook — the 'lost from an index' class becomes recoverable-by-construction with a demonstrated recovery.
integrate.note: C3 mandates it; making it a runbook (not just a test) means the first real torn-index incident has a rehearsed answer.

integrate.idea: Journal perf budget gate: time the healthcheck's v2–v5 walks journal-on vs journal-off with a hard regression budget (<5%); one appender per project, O(1) open-append-close, fsync policy configurable; per-tick/telemetry writes excluded from the taxonomy BY RULE (mutation-of-record boundaries only, per the C3 list).
integrate.note: FM-19: John already lived through one O(everything) dashboard regression; the budget makes 'dual-write is cheap' a measured claim.

integrate.idea: IPC contract table as a Stage-2 artifact: every dashboard↔job interaction (launch, tail-since, cancel, gate-answer, cost/rollup, swarm-register) gets a row with state owner, idempotency key, and defined behavior when EITHER side restarts mid-interaction — and the supervisor wave's stub-seam test matrix kills each side mid-interaction per row.
integrate.note: FM-7: the degrade-by-a-thousand-cuts failure is prevented by enumerating the cuts up front.

integrate.idea: Gate-answer durability: an AskUserQuestion answer is durably queued in the supervisor (persisted to the job dir) and ACKed before the dashboard POST returns — a dropped IPC hop is retryable, never lost; the stdin write happens supervisor-side against the handle it owns.
integrate.note: FM-7's worst cut isolated: gate answers are the one interaction where a silent miss wedges a live Foreman run.

integrate.idea: 'Restart mid-job → same job live, tail works, cancel works' as the LITERAL automated gate: a stub-seam test that restarts the dashboard side with a job in flight and asserts the restarted dashboard lists the SAME job_id as running, serves an advancing tail cursor, and can cancel it — plus the same script executed live as the sign-off.
integrate.note: FM-8: C4's second clause ('reporting it live') is the half that quietly fails; make it the gate's literal assertion.

integrate.idea: In-memory-structure rebuild table in the implementation plan: every dashboard-side structure (_LIVE, _JOB_DIRS, _ACTIVE_LANE, _FOLDER_BUILD, lane locks, SSE attach points) gets a rebuild-source column (durable record | supervisor query); any row with no rebuild source is a named design hole that must be resolved before EXECUTE.
integrate.note: FM-8: boot reconcile today 'reconciles death, never resumes life' — this table is the resume-life design forced into writing.

integrate.idea: Scripted supervisor service install: install_supervisor.ps1 does nssm install + ObjectName .\john + AppEnvironmentExtra cloned from the anchor service + CREATE_NO_WINDOW discipline — scripted, not documented — because the anchor service itself runs as .\john and claude.exe credentials live in John's profile.
integrate.note: FM-9: LocalSystem-default is the classic production-only failure; the memory file confirms the account fact (re-verified 2026-06-15).

integrate.idea: Two live healthcheck probes for the supervisor: (a) ask the LIVE supervisor to spawn a trivial claude.exe --version child and report output (credentials + PATH proven under the real service account); (b) restart the SUPERVISOR with a sacrificial child running and assert the child survived (job-object breakaway proven) — the inline seam covers logic only, never these.
integrate.note: FM-9: both failure modes are invisible to inline-seam tests by construction; only live probes can see them.

integrate.idea: ConPTY-across-processes spike scheduled Wave-1-adjacent and time-boxed, with the acceptance question written before it runs (latency bound, re-attach behavior, complexity budget) — so its answer shapes the supervisor sequencing instead of arriving after the supervisor waves have shipped.
integrate.note: Planning directive says EARLY explicitly; GAP-1 is the effort's one genuine unknown.

integrate.idea: Pre-designed fallback for the spike's 'no' branch, shipped in the SAME wave as the narrowing: a graceful pre-restart drain in the deploy script — close_session park + capture_session_docs + W3 warm-resume seed for every live PTY — so `nssm restart anchor` costs a warm reconnect, not dead context, for every remaining deploy of this very effort.
integrate.note: FM-10: the narrowing is a product decision, not a footnote; the drain reuses shipped machinery (crucible-improve W3/W6), so it's cheap.

integrate.idea: ANCHOR_SUPERVISOR=inline|external seam from day one: the supervisor's API is a Python interface with two implementations — in-process (tests, healthcheck, degraded mode) and loopback-HTTP client (production) — so the 4,970-line healthcheck and the test suite never need a second real process, and 'supervisor down' has a defined degraded behavior.
integrate.note: GAP-4 disposal; also gives FM-20 its supervisor off-switch for free.

integrate.idea: C4 live demo as a runbook artifact executed WITH John: a dedicated throwaway R&D project on the real service, a harmless long-running real job through the REAL launch path (fake_claude-driven), the exact elevated commands, expected observations, and rollback steps (supervisor stop + lane-lock clear); the criterion is honestly unmet until the runbook has run once.
integrate.note: FM-18: keeps the demo from either causing an incident or being silently skipped.

integrate.idea: anchor_md.py shared parsing module: extract the byte-identical twin parsers (anchor_gui 194–331 / anchor.py 127–178 plus the companion project/inbox/archived parsers) into one module imported by both, with a golden-corpus test (today's real markdown files parsed identically pre/post) as the de-fork gate.
integrate.note: C5 verbatim; byte-identical twins make this near-zero-risk, and the golden corpus proves it.

integrate.idea: Pre-deletion sweep for anchor_server.py: Get-ScheduledTask scan, Start-Menu/Desktop *.lnk target search for :5000/anchor_server, grep of _archive/ docs for instructions pointing at it — then delete with a one-line tombstone in the changelog.
integrate.note: FM-17: cheap, bounded, closes the off-repo-consumer class during the trust-building window.

integrate.idea: Path-audit tool for the data-dir move: scan every durable store (registry folder_path, worktree_path, discovery.json, job dirs, session records) for absolute paths under the repo root and emit a rewrite map; migration = stop service → migrate_data → path-rewrite → start → healthcheck as ONE scripted, rollback-able unit with the old dir preserved read-only for a week.
integrate.note: FM-11: paths.py's seam moves the ROOT but nothing rewrites the absolute paths already minted under it.

integrate.idea: Boot-reaper dry-run mode for the first post-move boot: worktrees.reap_orphans runs in report-only mode (ANCHOR_REAPER_DRYRUN) for the first boot after relocation, so path-resolution misses can't cascade into deleted parked-session worktrees; armed again only after a clean report.
integrate.note: FM-11's destructive tail: the reaper 'helpfully' deleting worktrees it can't match is the unrecoverable part.

integrate.idea: Git hygiene as its own commit + gate: git rm --cached the ~62 tracked runtime artifacts + .gitignore them (separate from the physical move), then a gate that runs a full healthcheck cycle and asserts `git status --porcelain` is empty — C6's 'stays clean' clause verified, not assumed.
integrate.note: FM-11: gitignore alone does nothing for TRACKED files; the two-step (untrack, then verify-through-a-cycle) is the honest closure.

integrate.idea: Cross-pillar dependency DAG with revert-compatibility as a stated Stage-2 rule: waves ordered so each merged wave is revertible WITHOUT reverting later-merged waves, tested by per-pillar off-switches — journal emission flag, auth warn/enforce flag, supervisor inline/external flag, static-vs-embedded frontend flag — making hybrid states named, supported configurations.
integrate.note: FM-20: 'never-broken increments' must hold for the SEQUENCE, not just per-wave; the flags make it testable.

integrate.idea: Healthcheck SLO in the plan: a wall-time cap and zero-known-flakes policy for the 5AM run; each new walk (parity gate, supervisor probes, cookie walk, relocated-data-dir walk) ships with its own quiescence strategy, retry-with-classification, and an 'Auto-fixes applied' degradation path — and runs 20× in nightly repetition before being wired into the 5AM run.
integrate.note: FM-15: a re-architecture FOR observability cannot afford to train John to ignore the red banner.

integrate.idea: Per-wave live-service smoke in the merge ritual: every wave's merge checklist ends with 'nssm restart anchor (or the drain script) → GET / 200 → one project window loads → healthcheck on-demand green' — a 5-minute scripted verification that C7 held on the box, not just in CI.
integrate.note: C7 is a property of the LIVE service; the suite alone can't see NSSM/env/port realities.

integrate.idea: Auth flips never ship in the same deploy as the JS that calls the flipped routes: a sequencing rule in the plan (frontend change lands, soaks; route enforce follows) so a half-cached client never meets a newly-gated endpoint.
integrate.note: FM-12's sequencing half, complementing the B-08 shim.

integrate.idea: Route-table introspection endpoint (/api/routes, token-authed): dumps the live table — path, method, auth policy, handler kind, legacy-or-migrated — giving the auth audit, the healthcheck, and eventually the Butler a machine-readable API contract.
integrate.note: Oranges: 2 steps ahead the Butler drives Anchor programmatically; the table-as-data makes the surface self-describing at near-zero cost since the table already exists as data.

integrate.idea: Journal tail CLI (`anchor.py rnd events <pid> [--since seq]`): a read-only inspection mirror over the per-project journal, following the established v3–v12 CLI-mirror convention — immediately useful for debugging dual-write, and the first taste of the journal as a queryable record.
integrate.note: Consistent with the repo's read-only CLI-mirror pattern; doubles as the reconcile-report viewer.

integrate.idea: Idempotent event replay tool: re-applying the journal against the legacy stores converges them (bounded, dry-run-first) — the operational answer to a legacy-ahead or conflict divergence classification.
integrate.note: Completes FM-6's mitigation: classification (B-22) without a repair verb leaves the on-call reflex dangerous; replay makes journal-ahead residue self-healing.

integrate.idea: Tail-cursor durability across supervisor restarts: the supervisor persists per-job read offsets/log positions in the job dir so /api/rnd/tail cursors survive a supervisor restart without resetting — covered by a row in the B-27 contract table and a kill-mid-tail test.
integrate.note: FM-7 named tail-cursor reset explicitly; job logs are already durable files, so the fix is offset bookkeeping, not new plumbing.

integrate.idea: Frontend extraction lands as MULTIPLE increments in dependency order — _PROJECT_WINDOW_JS first (raw string, zero interpolations, pure verbatim move), then the project-window HTML/CSS shell, then the generate_html f-string (the only genuinely fiddly one, gated on the B-01 census) — each independently merged, byte-gated, and live-smoked.
integrate.note: Sequencing by risk: the 4,660-line raw string is the cheap 25% of the shrink and proves the pipeline before the hard part; aligns C1 with C7's increment rule.

integrate.idea: Healthcheck consumes the route table for its endpoint walk: instead of a hand-maintained URL list, the 5AM walk iterates the declared rows (skipping kind=upgrade), asserting auth behavior per declared policy — new routes are automatically walked and an undeclared route can't hide from the daily check.
integrate.note: Oranges: couples C2's table to C7's healthcheck so the audit runs every morning, not once at review time.

integrate.idea: Named hybrid-state matrix in the plan: the supported combinations of the four pillar flags (e.g. 'frontend extracted + auth warn-only + journal on + supervisor inline') each get a one-line support statement and a healthcheck assertion of the CURRENT configuration, so mid-sequence reality is always a named state.
integrate.note: FM-20's 'hybrid state nobody fully understands' becomes impossible by naming; cheap because the flags exist per B-42.

grasscatcher.idea: Butler v0 prototype: a read-only daily digest agent that consumes the journal and posts 'what happened this week' summaries.
